title: The Great MOGGING of Bodybuilding: How Strength Came to DOMINATE Fitness
summary: A long history and polemic on how powerlifting rescued YouTube fitness around 2012 from PED-using bodybuilders' useless advice, then 'colonized' hypertrophy, so most natural bodybuilders now train like powerlifters and get torso-dominant, small-armed physiques. He attacks 'power copers', the term powerbuilding, and strength practices he says don't belong in bodybuilding (deloads, sandbagging, 5x5, hypertrophy blocks, mixed grip, competition lifts, minimalism, skipping isolation, dirty bulks), and calls for bodybuilders to reclaim their identity.
claims: Around 2009-2012 YouTube fitness was bodybuilding-centric, led by PED users who carried useless magazine advice over and recycled ideas that never worked for naturals
Early YouTube bodybuilding advice was machines, 20-rep sets, chase the pump, avoid bench and squat; he ran such a machine-only high-rep program for months with no results
Around 2012 powerlifting took over and brought advice that worked: focus on compounds, don't do endless reps, plan frequency so you can progress
He learned to squat from Candito, to deadlift and press from Alan Thrall, and to bench from Omar Isuf
Back then powerlifting programs gave better bodybuilding results than bodybuilding programs, so most aesthetics-minded lifters switched
Starting Strength reached cult status because huge numbers of people got their first gains from it
He considers 2012-2016, especially the Mark Bell / Super Training era, the golden age of YouTube fitness
Powerlifting influencers stay humble after success, while bodybuilding influencers turn into egotistical sellouts, because a vain pursuit attracts narcissists
Even today a medium powerlifting channel gives naturals better advice for getting big than a big bodybuilding channel
Nearly all the clickbait, gimmicks and bad information on fitness YouTube comes from the bodybuilding side
All the good programming principles on the platform come from strength sports, which built frequency, volume and intensity into their practice from day one
Big bodybuilding channels get their views from tourists who barely train, powerlifting channels from real lifters
Powerlifters who go on PEDs mostly keep their old training, while bodybuilders change their whole philosophy and then give advice that doesn't work for naturals
The last enhanced bodybuilder whose advice partly applied to naturals was John Meadows
Fitness trends are cyclical: the 2022 push to bulk rather than maingain repeats 2012
The claim that size equals strength oversimplifies; training for strength does not magically turn into size
Everyone should stay in their lane: powerlifters on strength, bodybuilders on hypertrophy; generalists who cover everything give worse information
He will never give strength advice: benching 255 lb, he has no business teaching people to bench more
AthleanX drifted from rehab to athleticism to bodybuilding; powerlifters checked him when he touched strength, but nobody defended hypertrophy
Influencers branch into many topics mainly as a business move to multiply their reach
He followed powerlifting principles for a long time: gains at first, then a plateau and lost direction, until he pivoted back to natural bodybuilding
'Power copers' are closeted bodybuilders who use strength as an excuse for poor muscle gains and are the main source of toxicity in strength communities
He learned the front squat from an Olympic weightlifter at his university gym and still front squats
The form police came from powerlifting's competition rules; for hypertrophy, an imperfect-depth squat or partial pull-up still builds muscle
Saying bodybuilding is 100% genetics is cope from people who ran Starting Strength for six years
Self-test: if a PR excites you most you care about strength; if a new muscle or vein in the mirror does, you care about looks. Five pounds on the bar means nothing to him
Power copers often pile on fat to get strong and then mock others for being weaker
Powerlifting influencers' imbalanced physiques, big torso and small arms, come from training built on the big three with little arm work, not genetics
Powerlifting is a sport judged on objective criteria; bodybuilding is an art judged subjectively, so the same tools must be used differently
Bench, squat and deadlift were used by bodybuilders before powerlifting adopted them; doing them doesn't make you a powerlifter
'Powerbuilding' is a meaningless marketing term; compounds plus isolation is simply how natural bodybuilders always trained
Train your arms as an afterthought and they will look like an afterthought
Natural powerlifters and natural bodybuilders look alike only because natural bodybuilders train like powerlifters
If you care about looks, call yourself a (natural) bodybuilder instead of hiding behind labels like powerbuilder
Deloads exist to prepare for or recover from a peak; bodybuilders never peak, so deloading only sacrifices tonnage and intensity. He never deloads
Leaving strength reps in reserve is a strength-athlete tool; bodybuilders who sandbag train for strength and shouldn't expect size
5x5 is not a good hypertrophy reference: too much sandbagging and too many low-value reps; evolving rep ranges that force failure are better
Bodybuilders shouldn't run hypertrophy blocks, since the whole program is hypertrophy; push strength with a small dose of strength work on the main compounds at the start of sessions
Mixed grip creates imbalances and injury risk; bodybuilders deadlifting for size should use straps
Competition specificity like paused bench, conventional deadlift and ass-to-grass squats makes no sense for someone who doesn't compete
Powerlifting-style minimalism strips out exactly what matters for a balanced physique
Don't skip isolation: chin-ups alone for biceps and bench alone for triceps leave arms small
Bulking to chase PRs mostly adds fat and better leverages, not quality muscle; he did it, then had to cut back down
Bro splits suck, but muscle-group splits like the gentleman split can work
Natural lifters across all strength sports should form a brotherhood of iron while respecting each other's different goals
